correctness.rationale: For the specified delete-first kernel, every off-diagonal exchange has a unique common deleted forest, giving equal forward and reverse rates, and each cut contributes the reciprocal of its host crossing count to the per-edge average Q(T). At stationarity two holds in succession have conditional probability Q(T)^2, giving covariance Var_pi Q. For a singleton side the only tree holds surely; for K_{2,b} the degree sum forces one two-edge hub path through the size-b side and b-1 peripheral edges. The crossing counts are b and 2, respectively, so the full four-cell law is constant conditional on the past, including b=1. This proves marked i.i.d., the binomial and geometric consequences, and, by the stated difference, the two minima b=4,5. For a,b>=3, a cut with x,y vertices from the two sides has x(b-y)+y(a-x) crossings. Applying this to the two displayed trees leaves the strictly positive difference [1/a+1/b-1/(a+d)-1/(b+d)]/(a+b-1), d=(a-2)(b-2). Both trees have positive uniform mass. A fresh exact connected-subset enumeration of K_{3,3} gave multiplicities 36,36,9 for 41/150,3/10,23/75 and variance 2/10125; only this finite constant depends on enumeration.
residual_risks: The stated negative result is proved at stationarity; no claim about correlation decay or independence from the entire tree trajectory is assessed.
